sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Vejle's central parking is run by the municipality with number-plate cameras and a free first two hours. The price page, last updated on 14 October 2026, lists for the plate-scanner car parks Albert, Tróndur and Cronhammar the first two hours free, then 9 kroner an hour, a day pass of 38 kroner, a monthly pass of 600 and an annual pass of 4,200; payment applies Monday to Friday 9:00 to 17:00 and Saturday 9:00 to 14:00, and other times and Sundays are free [0]. Abelones Plads, also scanned, is listed at 6 kroner an hour with no free period [1]. Surface lots with pay machines charge 9 kroner an hour, or 7.5 at Gunhilds Plads, with day passes of 45 to 54 kroner [2]. A driver who stays over two hours without an agreement or app can settle online within 72 hours; after that the owner receives an invoice with a 100-kroner fee [3].

Residents' permits are tied to the zone of the holder's address and cost 40 kroner a month in zones 1, 2, 5 and 6, while zone 3 residents' parking is valid only in Albert and Tróndur and costs 1,500 kroner for six months [4][5]. Holders of a disabled parking card park free in the four scanned car parks after registering their card [6]. The municipality lists four carpooling parking areas near the E45 motorway [16].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: We found no sourced plans for new or closed car parks. The notable provision is for electric vehicles: of the three municipal car park buildings, Cronhammar has 80 charging bays out of 400 spaces, by far the largest provision, while Albert has 10 and Tróndur 6; the pages do not name the operator or tariffs [7][8]. Cronhammar offers a weekend deal of 45 kroner from Friday after 17:00 to Monday 9:00, aimed at rail travellers from the station about 500 metres away [9]. The Tróndur building, known for its stained-glass stair tower, was acquired by the municipality in 2005 [17]. Some municipal car parks have sensors showing live availability on the municipality's parking map: green means more than 10 free spaces, yellow 5 to 10 and red 0 to 4 [11].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality operates three central car park buildings: Cronhammar (400 spaces), Albert (335) and Tróndur (269), about 1,000 spaces and 96 charging bays [7]. They use plate recognition at entry and exit with a 'Pay As You Go' registration or day, month and year passes [10]. Private operators fill the rest: Q-Park runs the 700-space Bryggen shopping centre car park with the first two hours free and no tariffs published online [12], and Steen & Strøm, which lists Bryggen among its malls, claims 700 parking places and 3 million visitors a year [13]. APCOA lists Dæmningen 23 as a 60-space private car park at 32 kroner per started hour [14].

Our data hold 13 Vejle car parks with about 2,800 spaces, but only three have more than a day of readings: Willy Sørensens Plads (249 spaces), Kirketorvet (37) and Volmers Plads (19), measured since 25 September 2026. Together they averaged about 45% on weekdays and at weekends. Kirketorvet, the small central pay-machine lot, averaged 69% and reached full in a single Wednesday-morning reading, while the large Willy Sørensens Plads averaged 41% and never exceeded 48%. The municipal car park buildings and Bryggen show only one early reading each, so we cannot yet say how full they are.
